purpose: Acquire registered galaxy photometry for the three RELICS clusters that already have local best-fit and 100-realization Lenstool convergence ensembles. The convergence maps are used only as model-dependent inverse targets for apparent dark-matter locations.

cross_validation.rule: Three leave-one-cluster-out folds. No target-cluster convergence pixels may set a forward-law parameter.

claim_boundary: The RELICS kappa maps are standard-lens-equation Lenstool reconstructions, not theory-independent observations.
The galaxy catalog is a stellar-light tracer, not a complete baryonic mass map; intracluster gas is absent from this first morphology test.
Inverse transport can describe paths that reproduce a target. Only held-out forward prediction can support a universal routing law.
The first stage tests spatial shape and source attribution. It cannot determine the absolute strength of redirected gravity without stellar-mass and gas calibration.
